target.title: fix(agent-core): bound harness exec stdout/stderr at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded stdout/stderr string accumulation in the agent harness `NodeExecutionEnv.exec()` method. Child process output uses `stdout += chunk` / `stderr += chunk` with no byte cap, so a runaway command can exhaust the agent process heap (OOM). Affects every agent exec call through `packages/agent-core`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `MAX_EXEC_OUTPUT_BYTES = 16 MiB` with a `maxOutputBytes` override on the shared `ExecutionEnvExecOptions` type. When output exceeds the cap, the overflowing stream is truncated and `[output truncated]` is appended, the process continues to natural exit. Key design decisions:

- **Per-stream independent truncation**: `stdoutTruncated` / `stderrTruncated` are tracked separately so stderr is not dropped after stdout crosses the cap
- **Byte-accurate trim**: `truncateToBytes()` iterates UTF-8 characters and stops at the exact byte boundary (not UTF-16 code units)
- **Shared contract**: `maxOutputBytes` lives on `ExecutionEnvExecOptions` so all `Shell` implementations share the same option

## User Impact

Runaway commands can no longer OOM the agent process. Normal commands are unaffected. The child process is left running after truncation.

## Real behavior proof

Proof script drives real `NodeExecutionEnv.exec()` against real child processes. Same script includes negative control.

**Environment:** Linux, Node 24, `node --import tsx proof-harness-exec-bound.mts`

**Fix (12 passed, 0 failed):**

```
[case 1] exec: 500-byte stdout with 64 KiB cap → full capture
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: exit code 0
  ok: stdout = 500 bytes
  ok: not truncated
  stdout: 500 bytes | exitCode: 0

[case 2] exec: 10 KB stdout with 1 KiB cap → truncated, process lives
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: exit code 0 (process not killed)
  ok: stdout truncated
  ok: stdout length <= cap + marker (~1100 bytes)
  stdout: 1043 bytes (capped at 1024) | exitCode: 0 | process healthy

[case 3] exec: 10 KB stderr with 1 KiB cap → truncated via stderr
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: stderr truncated
  stderr: 1043 bytes (capped) | stdout: 0 bytes

[case 4] exec: 2 KB stdout + 2 KB stderr with 1 KiB cap → both bounded
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: stdout or stderr truncated
  stdout: 1043 bytes (trunc=true) | stderr: 1043 bytes (trunc=true)  ← independent!

=== Proof Summary ===
default cap: 16 MiB | test cap: 1 KiB
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 12 passed, 0 failed
```

**Negative control (origin/main, same script):**

```
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 4 failed    ← truncation assertions FAIL
  FAIL: stdout truncated                    ← 10000 bytes accumulated (no cap)
  FAIL: stdout length <= cap                ← 10000 > 1200
  FAIL: stderr truncated                    ← 10000 bytes accumulated
  FAIL: stdout or stderr truncated          ← 2000+2000 unbounded
exit=1
```

## Evidence

### Vitest (real child process spawn)

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

### Changes addressed from review

| Finding | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| [P2] Shared truncation state drops stderr | `stdoutTruncated` + `stderrTruncated` independent flags |
| [P2] `chunk.slice(0,N)` slices by UTF-16 | `truncateToBytes()` iterates chars with `Buffer.byteLength` |
| [P3] `maxOutputBytes` not on shared type | Added to `ExecutionEnvExecOptions` |
